rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An act cannot issue when motives equally favor action and inaction; if one side prevails, its source either raises the same regress or is God, the first effective cause.
rows.anchor: الفعل الصادر من العبد إما أن يصدر عنه حال استواء الداعي إلى الفعل والترك أو حال رجحان أحد الطرفين على الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ashʿarite argument reads God's permission as will and creation: it cannot mean command or knowledge, since neither causes the transition from error to guidance.
rows.anchor: ولما بطل هذان القسمان لم يبق إلا أن يكون المراد من الإذن المشيئة والتخليق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An appeal to divine لطف does not evade the argument: if it does not tip action over inaction it cannot cause the result, and if it does, it necessitates the result.
rows.anchor: المراد بالإذن إما أن يكون أمرا يقتضي ترجيح جانب الوجود على جانب العدم أو لا يقتضي ذلك

words: لِتُخْرِجَ ٱلنَّاسَ مِنَ ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِ
rows.speaker: القائلون
rows.claim: Those who require instruction from a prophet and imam for knowledge of God infer that the Messenger's role in bringing people from disbelief to faith makes such teaching indispensable.
rows.anchor: القائلون بأن معرفة الله تعالى لا يمكن تحصيلها إلا من تعليم الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم والإمام

words: لِتُخْرِجَ ٱلنَّاسَ مِنَ ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that the Messenger only alerts people; knowledge itself is obtained through proof.
rows.anchor: أن الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم يكون كالمنبه ، وأما المعرفة فهي إنما تحصل بالدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural darknesses and singular light indicate many paths of ignorance and disbelief, while knowledge, faith, and guidance have one path.
rows.anchor: عبر عن الجهل والكفر بالظلمات وهي صيغة جمع وعبر عن الإيمان والهداية بالنور وهو لفظ مفرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parsing treats “to the path” as an apposition to “to the light,” with the governing preposition repeated; Razi compares Qur'an 7:75.
rows.anchor: إلى النور بتكرير العامل كقوله : { للذين استضعفوا لمن ءامن منهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “to the path of the Mighty, Praiseworthy” begins a fresh sentence answering the implied question, “To which light?”
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون على وجه الاستئناف كأنه قيل : إلى أي نور فقيل : { إلى صراط العزيز الحميد }

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila argue that right action requires an agent able to do all things, knowing all things, and independent of every need; otherwise incapacity, ignorance, or need could prompt evil.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : الفاعل إنما يكون آتيا بالصواب والصلاح ، تاركا للقبيح

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: In their reading, “Mighty” signals complete power and “Praiseworthy” God's deserving praise in all acts, which entails knowledge and freedom from need.
rows.anchor: فقوله : { العزيز } إشارة إلى كمال القدرة ، وقوله : { الحميد } إشارة إلى كونه مستحقا للحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The path is exalted and straight because it belongs to the deity who is Mighty and Praiseworthy.
rows.anchor: صراطا مستقيما للإله الموصوف بكونه عزيزا حميدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the preceding proofs that only God may be worshipped, the passage recounts Abraham's emphatic rejection of idol worship.
rows.anchor: لما بين بالدلائل المتقدمة أنه لا معبود إلا الله سبحانه وأنه لا يجوز عبادة غيره تعالى ألبتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks that Mecca be made secure. “Make this a town secure” asks that it join the secure towns; “make this town secure” removes its existing fear and gives it the opposite quality.
rows.anchor: سأل في الأول أن يجعله من جملة البلاد التي يأمن أهلها فلا يخافون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading واجنبني has three related Arabic forms. Al-Farrāʾ says the Hijaz uses the lightened جنبني يجبني, while Najd uses جنبني شره or وأجنبني شره.
rows.anchor: قرىء { واجنبني } وفيه ثلاث لغات جنبه واجنبه وجنبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root sense is to put one thing away from another, to a side or apart.
rows.anchor: وأصله جعل الشيء عن غيره على جانب وناحية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says Abraham asked for Mecca's safety, yet God did not grant it because people later destroyed the Kaaba and raided Mecca.
rows.anchor: أن إبراهيم عليه السلام دعا ربه أن يجعل مكة آمنا ، وما قبل الله دعاءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection asks why a prophet who never worships an idol would pray to be kept from doing so.
rows.anchor: أن الأنبياء عليهم السلام لا يعبدون الوثن ألبتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further objection says Abraham's prayer that his sons avoid idols was unanswered because Quraysh, among his descendants, worshipped idols; restricting “sons” to direct sons returns to the prophet objection.
rows.anchor: أنه طلب من الله تعالى أن لا يجعل أبناءه من عبدة الأصنام والله تعالى لم يقبل دعاءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer says Abraham prayed after building the Kaaba that the city be protected from destruction.
rows.anchor: أنه نقل أنه عليه السلام لما فرغ من بناء الكعبة ذكر هذا الدعاء ، والمراد منه : جعل تلك البلدة آمنة من الخراب

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes take “the town” to mean its inhabitants, as “ask the town” in Qur'an 12:82 means ask its people.
rows.anchor: أن المراد جعل أهلها آمنين ، كقوله : { واسئل القرية } ( يوسف : 82 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the inhabitants reading, Mecca has a special security: refugees are safe there, enemies meet without fear, and wild animals approach people there unlike elsewhere.
rows.anchor: ما اختصت به مكة من حصول مزيد من الأمن ، وهو أن الخائف كان إذا التجأ إلى مكة أمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer takes the request as a command and judgment that the town be secure, which was certainly fulfilled.
rows.anchor: وذلك الأمر والحكم حاصل لا محالة .

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj interprets the request as “keep me firm in avoiding idol worship,” like the prayer “make us Muslims for You” in Qur'an 2:128.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : معناه ثبتني على اجتناب عبادتها كما قال : { واجعلنا مسلمين لك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the question remains: if God certainly keeps prophets from idol worship, the request still needs an explanation.
rows.anchor: السؤال باق لأنه لأنه لما كان من المعلوم أنه تعالى يثبت الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham may have prayed despite knowing God would protect him, as an act of humility and an acknowledgment of constant need for divine grace.
rows.anchor: أنه عليه السلام وإن كان يعلم أنه تعالى يعصمه من عبادة الأصنام إلا أنه ذكر ذلك هضما للنفس وإظهارا للحاجة والفاقة إلى فضل الله

rows.speaker: الصوفية
rows.claim: Sufis distinguish manifest shirk, professed by idolaters, from hidden shirk: attachment of the heart to intermediaries and apparent causes; pure monotheism sees no agent besides God.
rows.anchor: شرك جلي وهو الذي يقول به المشركون ، وشرك خفي وهو تعليق القلب بالوسايط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi suggests Abraham's prayer may seek protection from this hidden shirk of relying on intermediaries.
rows.anchor: فيحتمل أن يكون قوله : { واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام } المراد منه أن يعصمه

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The author of al-Kashshāf says “my sons” means Abraham's direct sons; the prayer's benefit is the same as in his request for himself.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : قوله ( وبني ) أراد بنيه من صلبه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say Abraham meant all descendants then alive, both children and grandchildren; his prayer was certainly answered for them.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم أراد من أولاده وأولاد أولاده كل من كانوا موجودين حال الدعاء ولا شبهة أن دعوته مجابة فيهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says none of Abraham's descendants worshipped an image-idol; an aṣnām is an image, while an unfigured object is a wathan, and Quraysh worshipped stones and trees.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد : لم يعبد أحد من ولد إبراهيم عليه السلام صنما ، والصنم هو التمثال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects Mujāhid's distinction as weak: Abraham's prayer must concern worship of anything besides God, and stones are equivalent to idols for that purpose.
rows.anchor: وهذا الجواب ليس بقوي ، لأنه عليه السلام لا يجوز أن يريد بهذا الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer limits the prayer to believing descendants: those who do not follow Abraham's religion are not of him, as Noah's son was not of his family in Qur'an 11:46.
rows.anchor: أن هذا الدعاء مختص بالمؤمنين من أولاده والدليل عليه أنه قال في آخر الآية : { فمن تبعني فإنه مني }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God answered Abraham's general prayer for some descendants but not all; this does not diminish prophets, as God's covenant excluded wrongdoers in Qur'an 2:124.
rows.anchor: لعله وإن كان عمم في الدعاء إلا أن الله تعالى أجاب دعاءه في حق البعض دون البعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi's Ashʿarite proof infers that God alone turns people away from disbelief and toward faith, since Abraham asks God to keep him and his children from it.
rows.anchor: احتج أصحابنا بقوله : { واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام } على أن الكفر والإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilite interpretation that this asks for لطف is rejected as departing from the apparent meaning and from objections already given against that explanation.
rows.anchor: وقول المعتزلة إنه محمول على الألطاف فاسد ، لأنه عدول عن الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All theological schools agree that attributing misguidance to idols is metaphorical, because inanimate things cannot act; people go astray through worshipping them.
rows.anchor: واتفق كل الفرق على أن قوله : { أضللن } مجاز لأنها جمادات ، والجماد لا يفعل شيئا ألبتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever follows Abraham in religion and belief is “of him,” as close as a part of him; whoever disobeys him outside religion is entrusted to God's forgiveness and mercy.
rows.anchor: يعني من تبعني في ديني واعتقادي فإنه مني ، أي جار مجرى بعضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi argues that Abraham's request for forgiveness is intercession for major sinners among his community; its wording explicitly asks forgiveness and mercy for disobedient people.
rows.anchor: أن قوله : { ومن عصاني فإنك غفور رحيم } صريح في طلب المغفرة والرحمة لأولئك العصاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sinners cannot be unbelievers: Abraham had disavowed idolaters in his opening prayer, and “whoever follows me” implies nonfollowers are outside his religious community; the community agrees kufr's punishment cannot be removed by intercession.
rows.anchor: أنه عليه السلام بين في مقدمة هذه الآية أنه مبرأ عن الكفار وهو قوله : { واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording is unrestricted, so it cannot be narrowed to minor sins; minor sins and major sins after repentance are already obligatorily forgiven according to his opponents.
rows.anchor: لأن قوله : { ومن عصاني } اللفظ فيه مطلق فتخصيصه بالصغيرة عدول عن الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi concludes that the verse establishes intercession removing the punishment of major sins before repentance.
rows.anchor: فثبت أن هذه الآية شفاعة في إسقاط العقاب عن أهل الكبائر قبل التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Abraham had this station, Muhammad must have it: no distinction is recognized, its absence would diminish Muhammad, and Muhammad was commanded to follow Abraham (Qur'an 6:90; 16:123).
rows.anchor: أن محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم مأمور بالاقتداء بإبراهيم عليه السلام لقوله تعالى : { أولئك الذين هدى الله فبهداهم اقتده }

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says the phrase means whoever disobeyed Abraham and then repented; Razi rejects this restriction because it was already refuted.
rows.anchor: قال السدي معناه : ومن عصاني ثم تاب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says Abraham made this prayer before learning that God does not forgive associating partners; Razi rejects it because the context excludes intercession for disbelief.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن هذا الدعاء إنما كان قبل أن يعلم أن الله تعالى لا يغفر الشرك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says God is forgiving and merciful by transferring a person from disbelief to Islam; Razi objects that forgiveness and mercy imply dropping punishment, not conversion to faith.
rows.anchor: وقيل من عصاني بإقامته على الكفر فإنك غفور رحيم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view takes forgiveness and mercy to mean delaying punishment or death until sinners can repent; Razi rejects it because contemporary unbelievers are neither punished immediately nor regarded by Muslims as forgiven.
rows.anchor: وأما الرابع : وهو أن تحمل المغفرة والرحمة على تعجيل العقاب أو ترك تعجيل الإمانة فنقول هذا باطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among Abraham's requests, security comes first, showing it is the greatest blessing: religious and worldly interests cannot be completed without it.
rows.anchor: والابتداء بطلب نعمة الأمن في هذا الدعاء يدل على أنه أعظم أنواع النعم والخيرات وأنه لا يتم شيء من مصالح الدين والدنيا إلا به

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Asked whether security or health is better, a scholar chose security: a sheep with a broken leg eventually grazes again, but fear of a nearby wolf keeps it from eating until it dies.
rows.anchor: وسئل بعض العلماء الأمن أفضل أم الصحة ؟ فقال : الأمن أفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second request is for monotheism and protection from associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: والمطلوب الثاني : أن يرزقه الله التوحيد ، ويصونه عن الشرك ، وهو قوله : { واجنبني وبني أن نعبد الأصنام }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Some of my descendants” means a portion of Abraham's descendants: Ishmael and those born from him.
rows.anchor: فقوله : { من ذريتي } أي بعض ذريتي وهو إسماعيل ومن ولد منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The valley without cultivation is the valley of Mecca, containing no crops; the phrase “without crookedness” in Qur'an 39:28 is a parallel usage.
rows.anchor: وادي مكة { غير ذى زرع } أي ليس فيه شيء من زرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of “the sacred House” is that God forbade aggression and disrespect toward it and made the surrounding area sacred because of it.
rows.anchor: الأول : أن الله حرم التعرض له والتهاون به ، وجعل ما حوله حرما لمكانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation says it was always impregnable and feared by every tyrant, like something forbidden that must be avoided.
rows.anchor: أنه كان لم يزل ممتنعا عزيزا يهابه كل جبار كالشيء المحرم الذي حقه أن يجتنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation derives the name from its honored status and great inviolability.
rows.anchor: سمي محرما لأنه محترم عظيم الحرمة لا يحل انتهاكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth explanation says the House was protected from the flood, as the name al-ʿAtīq reflects its being freed from the flood's dominance.
rows.anchor: أنه حرم على الطوفان أي امتنع منه كما سمي عتيقا لأنه أعتق منه فلم يستعل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fifth explanation links the name to pilgrims being commanded to enter consecration, abstaining from things previously lawful to them.
rows.anchor: أمر الصائرين إليه أن يحرموا على أنفسهم أشياء كانت تحل لهم من قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sixth explanation says the site was made sacred at the creation of the heavens and earth, surrounded by seven angels; Adam built its counterpart, al-Bayt al-Maʿmūr, then it was raised to the seventh heaven.
rows.anchor: السادس : حرم موضع البيت حين خلق السموات والأرض وحفه بسبعة من الملائكة ، وهو مثل البيت المعمور الذي بناه آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A seventh explanation says people were forbidden to approach the House with blood, filth, and similar impurities.
rows.anchor: حرم على عباده أن يقربوه بالدماء والأقذار وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report recounts Sarah giving her servant Hajar to Abraham, Hajar bearing Ishmael, and Sarah asking Abraham to take the nursing child and mother away; he settled them at Mecca and entrusted them to God.
rows.anchor: روي أن هاجر كانت أمة لسارة فوهبتها لإبراهيم عليه السلام فولدت له إسماعيل عليه السلام

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said, “May God have mercy on Ismail's mother”; had she not hurried, Zamzam would have been a flowing spring.
rows.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( رحم الله أم إسماعيل لولا أنها عجلت لكانت زمزم عينا معينا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account continues that Abraham returned after Ishmael grew, and he and Ishmael raised the foundations of the House.
rows.anchor: ثم إن إبراهيم عليه السلام عاد بعد كبر إسماعيل واشتغل هو مع إسماعيل برفع قواعد البيت

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī regards much of the story as implausible: Abraham would not place his child where there was no food or water if another Syrian town was available, unless God had told him provisions would appear.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : أكثر الأمور المذكورة في هذه الحكاية بعيدة لأنه لا يجوز لإبراهيم عليه السلام أن ينقل ولده إلى حيث لا طعام ولا ماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says Zamzam's appearance could be an irhāṣ, a prophetic foretoken for Ishmael, which he permits; the Muʿtazila instead call it a miracle for Abraham.
rows.anchor: وأقول : أما ظهور ماء زمزم فيحتمل أن يكون إرهاصا لإسمعيل عليه السلام ، لأن ذلك عندنا جائز خلافا للمعتزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose phrase “so that they establish prayer” attaches to “I settled”: Abraham settled Ishmael and his children in the barren valley for prayer.
rows.anchor: واللام متعلقة بأسكنت أي أسكنت قوما من ذريتي ، وهم إسماعيل وأولاده بهذا الوادي الذي لا زرع فيه ليقيموا الصلاة

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī says hawā yahwī hawyan, with fatḥa, means to fall from a height to a lower place; other reported senses are to desire, hasten, descend, or come down toward them.
rows.anchor: قال الأصمعي هوى يهوي هويا بالفتح إذا سقط من علو إلى سفل . وقيل : { تهوى إليهم } تريدهم ، وقيل : تسرع إليهم

words: فَٱجْعَلْ أَفْـِٔدَةً مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ تَهْوِىٓ إِلَيْهِمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This prayer joins religious and worldly aims: people travel there for rites and obedience, and commerce brings livelihoods, expanding food, clothing, and general living conditions.
rows.anchor: أن هذا الدعاء جامع للدين والدنيا . أما الدين فلأنه يدخل فيه ميل الناس إلى الذهاب إلى تلك البلدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Some” is partitive: Abraham asks for the hearts of some people to incline toward his family.
rows.anchor: كلمة { من } في قوله : { فاجعل أفئدة من الناس تهوى إليهم } تفيد التبعيض

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says that if Abraham had said all people's hearts, Persians, Romans, Turks, and Indians would have crowded there.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد : لو قال أفئدة الناس لازدحمت عليه فارس والروم والترك والهند

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says that if Abraham had said all people's hearts, Jews, Christians, and Magians would have made pilgrimage; “some” means Muslims.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير : لو قال أفئدة الناس ، لحجت اليهود والنصارى المجوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying “some of the fruits” rather than “the fruits” indicates that Abraham asked for a portion of the fruits to reach them.
rows.anchor: أنه لم يقل : وارزقهم الثمرات ، بل قال : { وارزقهم من الثمرات } وذلك يدل على أن المطلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fruits may reach Mecca through trade, or through cultivation in nearby villages from which produce is brought.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون المراد بإيصال الثمرات إليهم إيصالها إليهم على سبيل التجارات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham seeks worldly provisions for his descendants so they can devote themselves to prayer, worship, and fulfilling their obligations.
rows.anchor: فإن إبراهيم عليه السلام بين أنه إنما طلب تيسير المنافع على أولاده لأجل أن يتفرغوا لإقامة الصلوات وأداء الواجبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After asking for his descendants' provisions, Abraham acknowledges that he does not know future outcomes; God knows their conditions, interests, and harms better than they do.
rows.anchor: وأنه تعالى هو العالم بها المحيط بأسرارها ، فقال : { ربنا إنك تعلم ما نخفي وما نعلن } والمعنى : أنك أعلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation says Abraham concealed his longing over separation from Ishmael and made his crying public.
rows.anchor: قيل : ما نخفي من الوجد بسبب حصول الفرقة بيني وبين إسماعيل ، وما نعلن من البكاء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation says he hid grief in his heart and refers publicly to his farewell exchange with Hajar: he said God would care for them; she asked whether God commanded it, and, hearing yes, said they need not fear.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ما نخفي من الحزن المتمكن في القلب وما نعلن يريد ما جرى بينه وبين هاجر

words: وَمَا يَخْفَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes the next clause as God's confirmation of Abraham, as in Qur'an 16:34.
rows.anchor: أنه كلام الله عز وجل تصديقا لإبراهيم عليه السلام كقوله : { وكذالك يفعلون } ( النحل : 34 )

words: وَمَا يَخْفَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Abraham continues speaking: nothing anywhere is hidden from the Knower of the unseen; the word min makes the statement exhaustive, not a single thing being hidden.
rows.anchor: أنه من كلام إبراهيم عليه السلام يعني وما يخفي على الذي هو عالم الغيب من شيء في كل مكان

words: ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِى وَهَبَ لِى عَلَى ٱلْكِبَرِ إِسْمَٰعِيلَ وَإِسْحَٰقَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an shows that God gave Abraham Ishmael and Isaac in his old age but does not specify his age; Razi cites reports giving Ishmael's birth at 99 and Isaac's at 112.
rows.anchor: فأما مقدار ذلك السن فغير معلوم من القرآن وإنما يرجع فيه إلى الروايات فقيل لما ولد إسماعيل كان سن إبراهيم تسعا وتسعين سنة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative report says Ishmael was born when Abraham was 64 and Isaac when he was 90.
rows.anchor: وقيل ولد له إسماعيل لأربع وستين سنة وولد إسحق لتسعين سنة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says Abraham had no child until he was 117.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير : لم يولد لإبراهيم إلا بعد مائة وسبع عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing is greater because old age is a time when one despairs of having children, so receiving them then fulfills a need after hope has faded.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكر قوله : { على الكبر } لأن المنة بهبة الولد في هذا السن أعظم ، من حيث إن هذا الزمان زمان وقوع اليأس من الولادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The birth of children at such an advanced age was a sign for Abraham.
rows.anchor: ولأن الولادة في تلك السن العالية كانت آية لإبراهيم .
